newsitem.title: USA: Big U.S. banks report earnings close to forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Big U.S. banks report earnings close to forecasts.

text.p: The biggest U.S. banks reported third-quarter earnings on or close to Wall Street estimates, although loss rates on credit card loans continued to creep higher.
Arthur Soter, analyst at Morgan Stanley & Co, said Chase Manhattan Corp and Citicorp, ranked first and second respectively based on assets, had "good, solid earnings and profitability."
He said credit card lending is getting considerable attention because it is virtually the only problem area for the banks.

"Credit cards will continue to be an issue that investors in these banks will have to contend with for a while longer," Soter said. He added that there is evidence the banks are slowing the growth of credit card portfolios, with solicitations down and standards raised. The tougher standards include shorter grace periods and higher late fees.

Chase Manhattan reported that the loss rate on domestic credit cards rose to $296 million or 4.95 percent of averaged receivables in the quarter from $279 million or 4.78 percent in the second quarter.
Citicorp said credit costs for its U.S. bankcards were $550 million or 5.11 percent of managed loans in the third quarter, up from $522 million or 4.99 percent in the second quarter.

First Chicago NBD Corp said card charge-offs in the third quarter were 5.9 percent, in line with the second quarter. Analyst Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman noted that First Chicago NBD's delinquencies in its card business continued to rise, with 4.3 percent of receivables past due by 30 days or more at the end of the third quarter versus 3.8 percent at the end of the second quarter.
